text:
amy_sales: Quick sync — Zenith verbally committed to an annual reserved deal but wants a tight POC before signing. Need capacity plan + pricing for POC. They say peak business-hour RPS ~1200 sustained, burst to ~5000 for 10–20m. Can we map to reserved GPUs + burst?

jordan_se: can you confirm expected avg tokens per request and model? chat or simple generation?

amy_sales: mostly chat (multi-turn), avg prompt+response ~1200 tokens, 95th latency SLO 300ms p95. They'll accept quantized models if quality holds.

mike_infra: rough sketch: for 1200 RPS at ~1200 tokens avg that's heavy. If we use a 70B quantized variant on A100-ish hardware, continuous reserved pool of ~8 GPUs + burst pool of 6 (spot) looks plausible. Burst handles the 5k spikes with queueing/backpressure.

jordan_se: 8 reserved + 6 burst seems like a starting point. Need more precise numbers: distribution of short vs long conversations, concurrency per user, KV cache hit expectation. Also which model latency profile (seq len matters).

amy_sales: Zenith says 60% of calls are short (<=400 tokens), 30% medium (400-1600), 10% long (>1600). KV cache reuse expected ~30%.

mike_infra: ok that helps. With 30% KV hit and mixed lengths our latency cost drops. Suggested autoscale policy: min=8 reserved, prewarm=2 per AZ, max-burst=6 spot GPUs, queue-limit 10k tokens, fallback model smaller Llama-13B for degradation.

mike_infra: example autoscale snippet:

```yaml
autoscale_policy:
  reserved_min: 8
  reserved_max: 12
  burst_pool: 6
  prewarm_per_az: 2
  queue_limit_tokens: 10000
  fallback_model: "llama-13b-quant"
```

jordan_se: also call out model version pinning and canary rollout for POC. We'll need performance traces for each commit.

nina_sre: security checklist — Zenith requires VPC peering, KMS for key management, and an admin audit log export. Private deployment preferred for POC if legal won't sign otherwise. Any data residency asks?

amy_sales: they're okay with hosted if we put them on a dedicated pool in their region, but legal_ops will push for KMS and audit logs.

legal_ops: flagged — we'll need to complete the security questionnaire before provisioning private. I'll take ownership of the questionnaire; can infra provide network + key management details by EOD?

mike_infra: yes. I'll compile network diagram, KMS integration steps, and perf runbook. ETA today EOD.

amy_sales: pricing Q — what's the ballpark monthly for the POC (1 month) with reserved 8 GPUs + ability to burst? They want a single-month quote to include burst credits and support.

mike_infra: ballpark compute cost = reserved 8 GPUs * 730 hours + burst usage estimate. Rough number: $120k–$180k for the month depending on spots and model choices. Add managed support + observability (~$12k). Final quote needs exact instance sizing.

jordan_se: propose to include a performance SLT (we'll measure p95, token cost) and a rollback plan that pins them to smaller model automatically if latency breaches SLO. Also include KV warmup script to reduce cold-start impact.

amy_sales: Zenith also asked about failover if reserved capacity saturated in region. Can we route to a secondary region with slightly higher latency?

mike_infra: yes, smart routing + fallback to stage in us-west if eu-west saturated. Need to ensure model versions replicated. Add cross-region prewarm to reduce cold starts — increases cost but reduces risk.

nina_sre: operations note — cross-region routing needs documentation for data transfer and DPA implications. Legal will check.

deploy-bot: [system] reserved-pool request created (req-789), status: pending infra review.

amy_sales: next steps — infra to produce: 1) perf sizing doc with final GPU count, 2) autoscale YAML, 3) network/KMS diagrams. legal to start questionnaire. I'll prepare a one-page POC scope (SLOs, duration, acceptance criteria).

mike_infra: will deliver docs by EOD and include a quick cost matrix (8/10/12 reserved tiers).

legal_ops: I'll ping Zenith for clarifications on DPA & KMS scope.

amy_sales: thanks team — can we reconvene tomorrow 10am PT for final sign-off before provisioning? :thumbsup:
